trigger: a Linux browser_policy file whose name contains bytes that are not valid UTF-8
summary: A non-UTF-8 policy file name landed verbatim in the row's source field. The command response travels in a protobuf string field and the receiver rejects the whole response on invalid UTF-8, so one such name dropped the host's entire browser_policy inventory instead of reporting a row for it. The SDK's own sanitize_utf8 was not enough: it only catches lone and truncated bytes and lets overlong forms, surrogates and code points above U+10FFFF through. Fixed in 476178de9: every free-text field now goes through a strict UTF-8 repair, each offending byte replaced with U+FFFD and flagged utf8_replaced in detail.

trigger: a host whose browser-policy files collectively exceed no stated total budget, since the per-file, per-directory and per-row caps are each independent and their product is not itself a bound
summary: The per-file, per-directory and per-row caps were each independent; their product was not an overall bound, so a host with enough policy content could make one collection run read an unbounded total of bytes. Fixed in 476178de9: the walk now also stops once it has read 16 MiB of policy files in one run (linux:byte_cap); rows already read stand and the result reports CONSTRAINED.

trigger: the real-plugin Linux dispatcher test asserting only an unconditional status rather than the shipped leg's actual output
policy_floor: CLAUDE.md / governance SKILL.md policy floor: a false-green test offered as closure evidence -- a test that cannot observe what it asserts
summary: The real-plugin Linux dispatcher test case asserted only an unconditional status, not that the shipped leg's rows, status, completeness, provenance and return code equal a direct run_linux_at call against the injected root, on the same host -- a false-green test that could pass even if the shipped leg diverged from its own implementation. A stale run_guarded comment also overclaimed that the suite exercised the plugin's call site. Fixed in 476178de9: the test now requires equality against the injected-root twin, so an unconditional status or a diverging leg fails on every Linux host, not only where a policy file happens to exist; the comment was corrected to match.

trigger: the FIFO hang guard and the raw-byte file-name test case in test_browser_policy_parsers.cpp closing their file descriptors by hand
policy_floor: CLAUDE.md / governance SKILL.md policy floor: manual resource cleanup in new C++ that is not RAII-wrapped
summary: The FIFO hang guard and the raw-byte file-name test case closed their file descriptors by hand, so a failed REQUIRE or a thrown exception between open and close leaked them -- new manual resource cleanup in C++ test code that was not RAII-wrapped. Fixed in 70650323a: both now use posix::Fd.

trigger: a Windows or macOS host (the not-yet-implemented legs), or a Linux host with an unreadable or unparseable policy file
summary: The typed result status is not returned by the server's response queries (REST, MCP, the dashboard), so a Windows or macOS host, or a Linux host with an unreadable or unparseable policy file, read as SUCCESS with empty output -- indistinguishable from 'no policy configured'. Fixed in b667b21ec: every outcome other than a complete read is now also written as one leading status row (status|-|-|-|policies|-|constrained-or-unavailable|-|reason), by the same seams that set the typed status; a complete read, including a genuinely absent policy set, still writes nothing. The macOS sample was recaptured to show the row.

trigger: dir_from_fd closing the directory descriptor by hand when fdopendir failed
policy_floor: CLAUDE.md / governance SKILL.md policy floor: manual resource cleanup in new C++ that is not RAII-wrapped
summary: dir_from_fd closed the directory descriptor by hand when fdopendir failed. Fixed in b667b21ec: it now takes the shared yuzu::agent::ScopedFd and hands it over only on success; the plugin's own private Fd class is gone.

trigger: a symlinked directory hop under the policy root, on Linux or macOS
summary: A symlinked directory hop reported linux:not_a_directory on Linux and macOS alike, because O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW on a symlink yields ENOTDIR -- the same errno as a genuine non-directory, so the reported reason misstated the real cause. Fixed in b667b21ec: open_dir_at now looks once more without following and reports linux:symlink_refused, matching what the README already claimed.

trigger: a wide policy JSON container -- many sibling child containers -- parsed with nlohmann's callback-based SAX interface
summary: nlohmann's callback parser is quadratic on a wide container of child containers -- a 1 MiB file took minutes -- and the existing depth cap was built on top of that same callback parser, on an ordinary collection path. Fixed in b667b21ec: the depth cap is now a linear pre-scan mirroring the parser's own comment rules (a line comment ends at LF, CR or NUL), followed by a callback-free parse; two needless vector and string copies on the row path were also removed.

trigger: docs/os-capability-matrix.md's prose stating a fixed plugin count
summary: The capability matrix's prose hard-coded a plugin count, which goes stale the moment another plugin merges -- the same class of staleness that later broke CI on a sibling workstream's raised PR. Fixed in b667b21ec, alongside the README no longer citing planning documents it cannot support or a sibling plugin that does not exist in this branch.

trigger: a policy value large enough that its row exceeds the server's per-chunk ingest cap -- e.g. a 1 MiB value of pipes escapes to 2 MiB, a 1 MiB array of floats dumps to 3.8 MiB
summary: One oversized policy value could make a row larger than the server's per-chunk ingest cap, which drops the row's source and detail fields while the agent still reports a complete read. Fixed in 1f8fbf23d: every free-text field is now cut at 64 KiB on a UTF-8 boundary, before escaping so a cut can never strand half an escape sequence in front of the field separator, and flagged truncated in detail.

trigger: a policy file containing many small ({}) JSON containers
summary: nlohmann parses a bare {} into about thirty times its three bytes, so the 1 MiB per-file cap alone still allowed roughly 30 MiB of parsed document per megabyte of {} content -- more than the existing comments and Resource Ledger claimed. Fixed in 1f8fbf23d: the linear pre-scan that replaced the callback depth guard now also counts containers; a file with more than 65536 containers is linux:json_too_complex and is not parsed. Measured worst case after the change: about 46 MiB resident for 16 files of one megabyte each, against 95 MiB before; the comments and Resource Ledger were corrected to match.

trigger: a max_rows value of SIZE_MAX, or a directory listed while being rewritten
summary: A max_rows of SIZE_MAX wrapped to 'build no rows' and read as an empty complete read rather than the caller's actual unbounded request; separately, a directory listed while being rewritten could return the same file name twice, presenting one file as two rows. Fixed in 1f8fbf23d: the row-budget arithmetic now saturates instead of wrapping, and returned names are de-duplicated. The typed-status call in run_guarded's handler was also confirmed to allocate and be guarded on its own -- the comment previously claimed more than the code did.

trigger: the two lines run_linux_at emits when a leading status row is present
policy_floor: CLAUDE.md / governance SKILL.md policy floor: a false-green test offered as closure evidence -- reversing the status row and the data row failed nothing before this fix
summary: The status row's position relative to the data row was never pinned by a test -- reversing the two lines in run_linux_at failed nothing before this fix. Fixed in 1f8fbf23d: a test now requires the status row to be the first line of the output. The same round added a differential case comparing the depth pre-scan against nlohmann's own SAX depth over 40000 generated inputs (so an nlohmann upgrade that changes a lexer rule fails the suite), a FIFO-at-a-directory-hop refusal test, and oversized-field, container-cap and unlimited-row-budget cases.

trigger: the committed Linux sample capture, after the leg's open, parse and status paths changed in the same round
summary: The leg's open, parse and status paths changed after the Linux sample was first captured, and the stamp's leg hash covers only the descriptor and columns, so the drift was invisible to that check. Fixed in b394c78f4: the sample was recaptured against the final leg -- body unchanged, four rows, OK/FULL -- with the date and the measured-privilege wording moved to the new capture.

trigger: the README Sensitivity paragraph's claim about RBAC-off dispatch of the browser_policy action
summary: The Sensitivity paragraph said RBAC-off let any authenticated session dispatch the browser_policy action; the legacy fallback actually still requires an admin session for a non-read operation regardless of RBAC -- only reading a stored result is that open. It also said the scope column never names a user without qualifying that as a Linux-only fact -- the planned macOS leg's own descriptor already documents per-user Managed Preferences. Fixed in 8271d283f, the third review round to find a wrong claim in this paragraph.

trigger: the memory-bound comments and Resource Ledger entry after the round-3 container cap landed
summary: After the round-3 container cap landed, the memory-bound comments still understated the real cost: a parsed document costs several times its text, and the appended row text costs several times that again -- on the order of a hundred MiB at the worst mixed shape, not the roughly 46 MiB an earlier, narrower measurement claimed; the field-cap comment's 'doubles' also understated a NUL-heavy field's threefold expansion. Fixed in 8271d283f: the comments and the Resource Ledger carry the correction, plus the two directory-listing callbacks the Ledger had left off.

trigger: a future contributor following the 'when a leg lands' checklist to update every site that still says planned
summary: The 'when a leg lands' checklist undersold itself as exhaustive, missing two sites that still said planned -- the privilege-model row and the yaml header comment. Fixed in 8271d283f: the checklist now says to grep for the remaining 'planned' text rather than trust a fixed list, and names the two sites it previously missed.
